_meta.description: Canonical navigation layout applied AFTER all manifest.d fragments merge (see applyMenuRelocations in main.js). Fragments stay the source of WHAT exists in the menu (ADR-037); this file is the single place deciding WHERE entries live. relocations: sourceId -> targetGroupId (groups dissolve into the target, leaves move under it, a child group targeting its own parent flattens) — this is how an entry is re-homed, and it MOVES navigation rather than deleting it. settingsSection: ids lifted into Nextcloud's settings foldout. removals: now EMPTY — see _removals_note for why the previous 160 entries were withdrawn; ADR-044 (no-functionality-loss) requires that retiring a menu entry leave its route reachable from some other surviving entry, which must be checked per id before this list is ever repopulated. Lives outside manifest.json because the app-manifest-v2 schema has additionalProperties:false at the root.

_settingsSection_note: Ids lifted into Nextcloud's settings foldout (the bottom-left gear / NcAppNavigationSettings, OUTSIDE the scrollable nav) by applySettingsSection in main.js — each becomes a flat top-level item with section:'settings'. This is the special settings position, not a normal menu group.
_removals_note: EMPTIED 2026-08-10 (gate-53 / ADR-044 no-functionality-loss). This list held 160 ids and its description called them 'leaf menu-entry ids retired as duplicate navigation'. Measured against the gate's own removals-invariant output, that was true of NONE of them: 140 were the ONLY menu entry reaching their route (ADR-044 errors — retiring them left the page with no navigation at all, reachable only by typing the URL), 11 matched no merged menu entry at all (warns — dead ids), and the remaining 9 were routeless GROUP HEADERS, not leaves. The 9 vanished only as a side effect: applyMenuRemovals never drops a node that still has children, so each was pruned by the empty-shell rule (children.length === 0 && hadChildren && !isClickable) once the 140 had taken all its children away. With the 140 restored, all 9 keep their children and are not dropped by any rule — verified by assembling with removals set to exactly those 9 and finding all 9 still in the menu — so every id in this list was either harmful or inert, and the list is now empty. Do not repopulate it without checking, per id, that another surviving menu entry reaches the same route; that check is what was missing, and it cost 140 pages their nav entry in a single change. relocations (above) is the mechanism for re-homing an entry — it moves navigation, it does not delete it.
